$comment: Authoritative attestation reference for the production publicai-gateway CVM. Fetched at runtime by the /proof page. composeHash was read back from the CVM's RTMR3 event log on 2026-09-02 and cross-checked against the Phala control-plane API; both report 342d0022. Image digests are the linux/amd64 children of the cosign-signed proof-v31 index for sub2api (INDEX c71a53c7) built by publish-tee-images run 33602101421 from commit 508253a07; the attestor image is deliberately left at its proof-v20 pin (INDEX cef1d03d) because deploy/attestor was not touched, and repinning it would widen the attested surface for nothing. VERIFICATION SCOPE, stated plainly: composeHash, osImageHash, the image digests and the build commit were each read back from a live source, and composeHash was cross-checked against two independent ones. The cosign keyless signature was NOT verified locally for this release - the workflow performs the signing and its run succeeded, and anyone can verify certificate identity https://github.com/FiiLabs/sub2api/.github/workflows/publish-tee-images.yml@refs/heads/feat/two-sided-market plus the embedded githubWorkflowSha against the sourceCommit below, but this file does not claim it was done. This release carries no application code change. It adds one data migration that recomputes the historical supplier earnings of a single internal account against the billing parameters now in force. Those entries were accrued under the earlier group multiplier and revenue share; the operator decided the history should follow the current parameters. The new basis is derived per entry from the official list price recorded on the corresponding usage log, so the result depends only on facts that can be checked today rather than on remembered configuration. The accrual rows themselves are rewritten rather than offset by a single correcting entry, because the thaw job moves money from frozen to available by summing the amounts on matured accrual rows: an offset alone would leave those rows at their old values and the balance would climb back over time. After the rewrite each row still satisfies basis times share equals amount, and the wallet's three figures are still the sums of the corresponding rows. One ledger entry records the operation with the parameters, the entry count and the before and after totals. The migration refuses to act when the wallet has any activity other than accruals and thaws, since the balance then cannot be recomputed from accruals; it skips rather than raising, because the migration runner is fail-closed and an exception here would keep the container from starting. It was rehearsed against a restored copy of the production database using the real migration runner: the wallet matched the rows, a forced full thaw produced no rebound, a second run was refused by the guard, other suppliers were untouched, and a fresh install skips it entirely. proof-v30 was built from a commit that was subsequently amended and removed from the branch, and was skipped. Earlier in this line: proof-v29 (referral copy pricing), v28 (audience-specific films on the landing page, Fable 5.1 copy), v27 (footer contact rail), v26 (upstream sync through v0.1.185 and beyond, Claude Fable 5.1), v24 (pricing copy at 14 percent and a 50 percent revenue share), v23, v22, v21, v20, v19, v18, v17, v16/v15. osImageHash, appId and instanceId are unchanged; the deploy passed --no-dev-os explicitly, because phala deploy silently switches to a dev OS image when it detects a local SSH key and a dev OS would void the attestation, and the control plane confirms is_dev false after the rollout. A full postgres backup was taken and verified immediately beforehand - downloaded from S3, gzip-tested, 110 COPY sections - and it is the rollback point for the data change. This rollout completed in 81 seconds with no incident.
